_why: 2026-10-04, row T of HemaSuite's anemia-jmj triage. During Phase 5 the codex gate refused every shell command outside its test/read-only/control allowlist anywhere in the project, so a manuscript run unrelated to the feature needed the feature's state paused and restored. The operator may now list argv prefixes in `.h-mad/phase5-shell-allow`. Each row removes one limit on that admission, or the admission itself, or the guard that keeps codex from writing the file.

mutations.name: allowance-never-consulted
mutations._mechanism: The admission never fires, which is the defect: a declared manuscript run is still refused during an unrelated Phase 5.

mutations.name: lexical-subset-dropped
mutations._mechanism: Without the lexical subset, `&&`, `>` and the like reach shlex as ordinary tokens after a declared prefix, so a declared prefix carries any second command.

mutations.name: executable-not-resolved
mutations._mechanism: A declared name is admitted even when nothing on PATH answers to it, so the decision no longer depends on what would actually run.
mutations.find: if not argv or shutil.which(argv[0]) is None:  # M:SA-RESOLVE

mutations.name: prefix-reduced-to-executable
mutations._mechanism: Matching only the executable turns `hpw manuscript run` into `hpw *`, admitting every subcommand of a declared tool.
mutations.find: return any(argv[:len(prefix)] == prefix for prefix in prefixes)  # M:SA-PREFIX
mutations.replace: return any(argv[:1] == prefix[:1] for prefix in prefixes)  # M:SA-PREFIX

mutations.name: malformed-line-skipped
mutations._mechanism: A line that cannot be parsed is skipped instead of refusing, so a half-broken allowance silently admits whatever its parsable lines say.
mutations.find: return f"{SHELL_ALLOW_FILE}:{number} cannot be parsed ({exc})"  # M:SA-PARSE

mutations.name: unreadable-read-as-empty
mutations._mechanism: An allowance that cannot be read is treated as declaring nothing, so 'I could not read it' and 'it lists nothing' take the same branch.

mutations.name: codex-may-write-the-allowance
mutations._mechanism: Without the write guard a worker writes `.h-mad/phase5-shell-allow` (a non-Python write inside the root) and grants itself any command.
mutations.find: if phase5_status in {"active", "unknown"} and _is_shell_allowance(root, resolved):  # M:SA-GUARD
mutations.replace: if phase5_status in {"active", "unknown"} and False:  # M:SA-GUARD

mutations.name: guard-is-case-sensitive
mutations._mechanism: On a case-insensitive filesystem `.H-MAD/Phase5-Shell-Allow` is the same file the gate reads, so a case-sensitive comparison lets a respelling through.

mutations.name: guard-outlives-phase5
mutations._mechanism: The guard fires with no feature at step5, so the operator's own codex session cannot maintain the file between features.
mutations.find: if phase5_status in {"active", "unknown"} and _is_shell_allowance(root, resolved):  # M:SA-GUARD
